subject: biology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: A cell divides by mitosis. How many daughter cells are produced?
questions.explain: Mitosis produces two daughter cells from a single parent cell.

questions.q: The daughter cells produced by mitosis are:
options: Genetically identical to the parent cell
Genetically different from the parent cell
Cells with half the number of chromosomes
questions.explain: Mitosis produces genetically identical diploid daughter cells.

questions.q: Which process in the body relies on mitosis?
questions.explain: Mitosis is used for growth, repair and replacement of cells.

questions.q: What is the correct order of the stages of mitosis?
questions.explain: Mitosis proceeds as prophase, metaphase, anaphase then telophase.

questions.q: What happens during interphase, before mitosis begins?
options: The DNA is copied and the number of subcellular structures increases
Chromosomes line up along the equator of the cell
questions.explain: During interphase the DNA replicates and organelles are duplicated ready for division.

questions.q: A human body cell contains 46 chromosomes. How many chromosomes will each daughter cell contain after mitosis?
questions.explain: Mitosis maintains the chromosome number, so each daughter cell has 46.

questions.q: A stem cell is best described as:
options: An undifferentiated cell that can divide to produce specialised cells
A cell that has already specialised for one job
A cell that is unable to divide
A cell that contains no nucleus
questions.explain: Stem cells are undifferentiated and can divide and differentiate into specialised cells.

questions.q: In plants, stem cells are found in tissue called:
questions.explain: Plant stem cells are located in meristems, found in the tips of roots and shoots.

questions.q: Why are embryonic stem cells more useful than adult stem cells for many treatments?
options: They can differentiate into any type of cell
questions.explain: Embryonic stem cells can differentiate into any cell type, whereas adult stem cells are more limited.

questions.q: One risk of using stem cells in medical treatment is that:
options: The cells may divide uncontrollably and form a tumour
The cells always cure the disease
The cells cannot divide at all
The cells contain no genetic material
questions.explain: A risk of stem cell therapy is uncontrolled division leading to tumour formation.

questions.q: A patient's pancreas can no longer produce insulin. How might stem cells help treat this condition?
options: By differentiating only into nerve cells
By stopping all cell division in the body
questions.explain: Stem cells could differentiate into functioning insulin-producing pancreatic cells.

questions.q: The central nervous system (CNS) consists of:
questions.explain: The CNS is made up of the brain and the spinal cord.

questions.q: Which type of neurone carries impulses from the CNS to an effector?
questions.explain: Motor neurones carry impulses from the CNS to effectors such as muscles or glands.

questions.q: Which shows the correct pathway of a nervous response?
options: Stimulus, receptor, sensory neurone, CNS, motor neurone, effector
Stimulus, effector, CNS, receptor, sensory neurone
Receptor, stimulus, motor neurone, CNS, effector
Effector, motor neurone, CNS, sensory neurone, receptor
questions.explain: A stimulus is detected by a receptor and passed via sensory neurone, CNS and motor neurone to an effector.

questions.q: How is an impulse transmitted across a synapse?
options: A neurotransmitter chemical diffuses across the gap
An electrical impulse jumps directly across the gap
The two neurones touch and pass the impulse on
The blood carries the impulse across the gap
questions.explain: At a synapse a neurotransmitter diffuses across the gap to the next neurone.

questions.q: Why does a reflex action happen faster than a normal response?
options: It does not involve the conscious part of the brain
It uses a greater number of neurones
It requires the person to think first
questions.explain: Reflexes are rapid because they bypass the conscious brain, protecting the body from harm.

questions.q: You touch a hot object and pull your hand away before you feel any pain. This is an example of:
questions.explain: Pulling away before feeling pain is a protective reflex action controlled by a reflex arc.

questions.q: Which part of the brain controls unconscious activities such as heart rate and breathing?
questions.explain: The medulla oblongata controls unconscious activities like heart rate and breathing.

questions.q: A patient has damage that causes poor balance and uncoordinated movement. Which part of the brain is most likely affected?
options: The language area of the cerebrum
questions.explain: The cerebellum coordinates movement and balance, so damage causes clumsy, uncoordinated movement.

questions.q: How can scientists investigate the function of different regions of the brain?
options: By using CT and PET scans or studying patients with brain damage
By dissecting the spinal cord only
By measuring the patient's blood sugar levels
By counting the chromosomes in brain cells
questions.explain: Brain function is studied using CT and PET scans and by examining patients with brain damage.
